key_insight: In this Northwestern Russia registry study, cancer patients who received at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose had better overall survival than unvaccinated patients.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest vaccination may be an important survival-associated preventive measure for cancer patients, especially those at higher risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes.
method: Retrospective population-based cohort linking cancer registry, vaccination records, and AI-analyzed chest CT data.
Primary landmark survival analysis among patients alive on March 1, 2021, with multivariable Cox adjustment.
Sensitivity analysis repeated with a later landmark date to reduce immortal time bias.
evidence_signal: Among 1,144 cancer patients, only 6.6% were vaccinated, and vaccination was associated with improved 3-year overall survival and a lower adjusted mortality hazard.
watch_item: Because this is observational registry research, residual confounding and selection differences between vaccinated and unvaccinated patients may still influence the association.
paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
